stacks.title: Stacks
stacks.description: Each goroutine carries a stack of work trays. Call a helper repeatedly and watch a tray arrive for each active call, then leave on return.
stacks.html:
Each goroutine carries a stack of work trays. Call a helper repeatedly and watch a tray arrive for each active call, then leave on return.

  • Count how many sum frames are on the stack at the deepest point
  • Explain why each sum frame has its own n
  • Say in what order the frames leave the stack

escape-analysis.title: Escape analysis
escape-analysis.description: A value that leaves its room needs an address that still works later. Return a pointer, then follow it after the creating call has ended.
escape-analysis.html:
A value that leaves its room needs an address that still works later. Return a pointer, then follow it after the creating call has ended.

  • Say why x must outlive the makeValue call
  • Find the value the stage marks as moved to the heap
  • Say that escape analysis happens when the program is compiled

allocation.title: Allocation
allocation.description: An allocation request is like asking a stockroom for a box that fits. Compare the requested size with the class of box the model selects.
allocation.html:
An allocation request is like asking a stockroom for a box that fits. Compare the requested size with the class of box the model selects.

  • Say what a size class is in one sentence
  • Explain why a 13-byte request may use a slightly bigger slot
  • Compare each requested size with the heap object the stage draws

garbage-collection-basics.title: Garbage collection basics
garbage-collection-basics.description: A collector is a librarian following bookmarks from the books still in use. Remove the last bookmark, then inspect which books remain reachable.
garbage-collection-basics.html:
A collector is a librarian following bookmarks from the books still in use. Remove the last bookmark, then inspect which books remain reachable.

  • Name the root that keeps the new(int) box alive at first
  • Say why keep = nil alone does not free anything
  • Predict which heap objects survive runtime.GC()

gc-pacing-and-tuning.title: GC pacing and tuning
gc-pacing-and-tuning.description: GC tuning is a budget dial, not a faster-cleanup button. Run the same allocation pattern under different model settings and compare memory room with…
gc-pacing-and-tuning.html:
GC tuning is a budget dial, not a faster-cleanup button. Run the same allocation pattern under different model settings and compare memory room with collection work.

  • Say what SetGCPercent trades: memory room against GC work
  • Explain why a smaller budget can mean more GC work, not less
  • Say why the program restores the old setting at the end

memory-friendly-go-and-leaks.title: Memory-friendly Go and leaks
memory-friendly-go-and-leaks.description: A tiny window can keep a whole warehouse in use. Keep a short slice, then copy what you need and compare the retention paths.
memory-friendly-go-and-leaks.html:
A tiny window can keep a whole warehouse in use. Keep a short slice, then copy what you need and compare the retention paths.

  • Say why cap(small) is 64 when len(small) is only 2
  • Explain how a 2-item slice can keep 64 ints alive
  • Use copy to keep only the items you need
